claims.text: OCHA's oPt Humanitarian Situation Report (23 July 2026) states: 'Fatalities linked to settler attacks in 2026 have already surpassed the total recorded during all of 2025, with 18 Palestinians killed as of 20 July compared with 17 throughout 2025,' and 'about 90 Palestinians were displaced by demolitions and settler attacks during the reporting period, most following a large-scale demolition carried out by Israeli authorities in a Bedouin community in Qalqiliya governorate.'

Human Rights Watch (hosted on ReliefWeb): 'Two Israeli settler attacks on Tal village near Nablus in the West Bank on July 24, 2026, resulted in the killing of four Palestinians and two Israelis... The July 24 killings in Tal bring the Palestinian death toll in the occupied West Bank since July 19 to 10.' The incident triggered a wave of settler reprisal attacks on nearby Palestinian villages and the Israeli government's announcement of a 'major counterterrorism operation.'

Per the same ReliefWeb-hosted Human Rights Watch report: 'As of July 19, the United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) reported 68 Palestinians killed in the West Bank in 2026, at least 13 by settlers. OCHA reported that as of July 15, 20 Israelis had been injured in 2026 in the West Bank.'

UN News, citing OHCHR and OCHA (29 July 2026): 'As of 24 July, the agency reports that 76 Palestinians and one Israeli have died this year in settler attacks... Since Friday, eight Palestinians, including a boy, and two members of the Israeli military have also been killed in the region.' 'The number of settler attacks has increased each year since 2023... rising to 1,835 last year.' 'There were about 190 attacks per month in the first four months of 2026, putting the West Bank on a trajectory to reach more than 2,000 attacks by the end of the year.' 'Nearly 700 Palestinians in nine communities in the West Bank were displaced as a result of settler attacks in the first four months of 2026.'

UN News (29 July 2026), citing OHCHR and OCHA: 'As of 24 July, the agency reports that 76 Palestinians and one Israeli have died this year in settler attacks... Since Friday, eight Palestinians, including a boy, and two members of the Israeli military have also been killed in the region.' The article describes West Bank settler violence as having hit an 'all-time high.' It also reconfirms OCHA's separate figure that 18 Palestinians died in 2026 as of 20 July in attacks involving settlers (12 by settlers, 3 by Israeli forces, 3 disputed responsibility), and repeats the 'nearly 700 Palestinians across nine communities' displacement figure for the first four months of 2026.

description: A sharp escalation of Israeli settler violence in the occupied West Bank culminated on 24 July 2026 when Israeli settlers carried out two attacks on Tal village near Nablus, leaving four Palestinians (two brothers and two cousins from the Ramadan family) and two Israelis dead, and triggering a wave of settler reprisal attacks on nearby Palestinian villages, mosque burnings, and an Israeli government-announced 'major counterterrorism operation.' The attack capped a week of escalating violence: OCHA reported 68 Palestinians killed in the West Bank in 2026 as of 19 July (at least 13 by settlers), rising to about 10 Palestinian deaths in the week since 19 July alone, while fatalities linked specifically to settler attacks in 2026 (18 as of 20 July) had already surpassed the full-year 2025 total of 17. A newer OHCHR figure reported via UN News on 29 July 2026 puts settler-attack fatalities substantially higher — 76 Palestinians and 1 Israeli killed in settler attacks so far in 2026 as of 24 July, on a trajectory to exceed 2,000 settler attacks for the year (up from 1,835 in 2025), with nearly 700 Palestinians displaced across nine West Bank communities in the first four months of 2026 alone. The same UN News report states that, since 24 July, a further eight Palestinians (including a child) and two Israeli military members have been killed, describing West Bank settler violence as having hit an 'all-time high.' This OHCHR count and OCHA's 18-killed figure appear to use different methodologies or scopes and have not been reconciled by an authoritative source. The violence is occurring amid a fragile Gaza ceasefire and continued deterioration of humanitarian conditions across the Occupied Palestinian Territory.

impact.summary: The 24 July settler attacks on Tal village near Nablus killed 4 Palestinians and 2 Israelis and brought the West Bank Palestinian death toll since 19 July to 10 (per Human Rights Watch, hosted on ReliefWeb). OCHA reported 68 Palestinians killed in the West Bank in 2026 as of 19 July (at least 13 by settlers) and 20 Israelis injured in 2026 as of 15 July. A newer OHCHR figure reported via UN News (29 July 2026) puts 2026 settler-attack fatalities as of 24 July at 76 Palestinians and 1 Israeli, alongside about 190 settler attacks per month in the first four months of 2026 (on pace to exceed 2,000 for the year, up from 1,835 in 2025) and nearly 700 Palestinians displaced across nine communities in that four-month window. The same UN News report (29 July 2026) states that, since 24 July, a further eight Palestinians (including a child) and two Israeli military members have been killed, and describes West Bank settler violence as having reached an 'all-time high.' The OHCHR and OCHA settler-attack death tolls have not been reconciled by an authoritative source.
